q.t: 1 metre = how many centimetres?
q.e: A metre scale is marked into 100 equal small parts, and each part is 1 cm.

q.t: Half a metre (1/2 m) = how many centimetres?
q.e: Half of 100 cm is 50 cm.

q.t: A quarter metre (1/4 m) = how many centimetres?
q.e: Split 100 cm into 4 equal parts: 25 cm each.

q.t: 2 m = how many centimetres?
q.e: Each metre is 100 cm, so 2 metres are 100 + 100.

q.t: Which unit is best for measuring an eraser?
q.e: An eraser is much shorter than a metre, so we use the small unit, cm.

q.t: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a classroom?
q.e: A classroom is many metres long; counting centimetres would take far too long.

q.t: 1 m 20 cm = how many centimetres?
q.e: 1 m is 100 cm, and 20 cm more makes 120 cm.

q.t: The perimeter of a shape is:
q.e: Perimeter is the distance all the way round the edge.

q.t: A square on a 1 cm dot grid has sides of 3 cm. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
q.e: Walk round all 4 sides: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3.

q.t: 400 cm = how many metres?
q.e: Every 100 cm makes 1 metre, and 400 has four hundreds.

q.t: 4 m 60 cm = how many centimetres?
q.e: 4 m is 400 cm, plus 60 cm is 460 cm.

q.t: 550 cm is the same as:
q.e: 500 cm make 5 m, and 50 cm are left over.

q.t: A board is 2 m long. Each border sticker is 20 cm long. How many stickers cover the length exactly?
q.e: 2 m is 200 cm, and 200 cm holds 10 lengths of 20 cm.

q.t: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
q.e: Go round all four sides: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3.

q.t: Three quarter-metre ropes are laid end to end. How long are they together (in cm)?
q.e: Each quarter metre is 25 cm: 25 + 25 + 25.

q.t: Two half-metre ropes joined end to end make:
q.e: Two halves make a whole: 50 cm + 50 cm = 100 cm.

q.t: Ashwin’s scale is broken. A pencil starts at the 3 cm mark and ends at the 11 cm mark. How long is the pencil (in cm)?
q.e: Count the gaps between the marks: from 3 to 11 is 8 centimetres.

q.t: A triangle has sides 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
q.e: Add the lengths of all the sides.

q.t: Which is longer: 1 m 40 cm or 140 cm?
q.e: 1 m 40 cm = 100 cm + 40 cm = 140 cm — two ways of writing the same length.

q.t: 6 m = how many centimetres?
q.e: 6 groups of 100 cm.

q.t: Ramu is 1 m 25 cm tall and Shamu is 118 cm tall. How much taller is Ramu (in cm)?
q.e: Change Ramu’s height to cm first: 125 cm − 118 cm = 7 cm.

q.t: A square garden has sides of 5 m. How much fencing goes all the way round it (in m)?
q.e: The fence follows the boundary: 4 sides of 5 m.

q.t: A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. How long is each side (in cm)?
q.e: A square has 4 equal sides sharing the 20 cm: 20 ÷ 4.

q.t: Your hand is 15 cm long. A desk is 6 hand-lengths long. How long is the desk (in cm)?
A whale is about 30 m long and a crocodile is about 6 m long. About how many crocodiles laid end to end match the whale?
q.e: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 — five lengths of 6 m reach 30 m.

q.t: 3 m 5 cm = how many centimetres?
q.e: 3 m is 300 cm, and 5 cm more is 305 — not 350!

q.t: In the long jump, Ali jumped 1 m 15 cm and Sara jumped 98 cm. How much farther did Ali jump (in cm)?
q.e: Ali’s jump is 115 cm, and 115 − 98 = 17.

q.t: On a 1 cm grid, a rectangle is 4 cm by 2 cm and a square is 3 cm by 3 cm. Which has the longer boundary?
q.e: Rectangle: 4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12 cm. Square: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 cm.

q.t: A 5 m rope is cut into pieces of 50 cm each. How many pieces?
q.e: 5 m is 500 cm, and each metre gives 2 half-metre pieces: 5 × 2 = 10.

q.t: 1/2 m and 1/4 m of rope are joined. How long is the rope (in cm)?
q.e: 1/2 m is 50 cm and 1/4 m is 25 cm.

q.t: A ribbon is 3 m long. Priya cuts off 1 m 40 cm and then 85 cm. How much ribbon is left (in cm)?
q.e: Change everything to cm: 300 − 140 = 160, then 160 − 85 = 75.

q.t: A park is a rectangle 25 m long and 15 m wide. Asha walks round it twice. How far does she walk (in m)?
q.e: Once round is 25 + 15 + 25 + 15 = 80 m, so twice round is 160 m.

q.t: A rectangular garden is 8 m long and 5 m wide. A fence goes all round except a 1 m gate. How long is the fence (in m)?
q.e: The whole boundary is 26 m, and the gate leaves 1 m without fence.

q.t: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Its long side is 7 cm. How long is its short side (in cm)?
q.e: The two long sides use 14 cm; the other 6 cm is shared by two short sides: 3 cm each.

q.t: Chutki’s plant is 12 cm tall. It grows 2 cm every week. How tall is it after 4 weeks (in cm)?
q.e: In 4 weeks it grows 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 cm, and 12 + 8 = 20.

q.t: A border sticker is 25 cm long. How many stickers go all the way round a square board with 1 m sides?
q.e: Each 1 m side takes 4 stickers of 25 cm, and there are 4 sides: 4 × 4.

q.t: An ant walks once round the edge of a rectangle 5 cm long and 2 cm wide. How far does it walk (in cm)?
q.e: The ant walks the perimeter: 5 + 2 + 5 + 2.

q.t: Three children are 1 m 32 cm, 128 cm and 1 m 9 cm tall. How much taller is the tallest than the shortest (in cm)?
q.e: In cm they are 132, 128 and 109 (1 m 9 cm is 109, not 190). 132 − 109 = 23.

q.t: Toy cars rolled down a ramp: Car 1 went 2 m 10 cm, Car 2 went 185 cm, Car 3 went 1 m 98 cm. Which car came second?
q.e: In cm: Car 1 = 210, Car 3 = 198, Car 2 = 185. Car 3 is in the middle.

q.t: Lace 2 m long is sewn round the edge of a tablecloth 60 cm long and 40 cm wide. How much lace is left over (in cm)?
q.e: The edge is 60 + 40 + 60 + 40 = 200 cm, exactly the 2 m of lace — nothing is left.
